metric.semantic_locality.basis_disclosure: This figure is computed on Quidra's own all-fragments basis (39 of 44 probes) because this work unit is a single-language shard and the common cross-language basis (probes where all 10 languages have a fragment) can only be determined once every language shard's capability-support results are merged by the runner. The runner is responsible for recomputing the common-basis figure across all languages per capability_universe.json interaction_with_quality_metrics.common_basis_rule before final aggregation; this evidence block records Quidra's raw per-probe lookup counts so that recomputation is possible without re-deriving them.
metric.semantic_locality.exclusion_rule: Per capability_universe.json interaction_with_quality_metrics.common_basis_rule and na_policy NA-2/NA-4, a probe for which Quidra has NO fragment at all (capability NONE/UNSUPPORTED) contributes to Capability Coverage's denominator but is excluded from the semantic-locality raw-measurement basis because no lookup count can be taken for a nonexistent fragment. Five probes were judged UNSUPPORTED for Quidra under the frozen language spec: F05.P3 (Quidra function values are explicitly capture-free per architecture.md/language.md 'Function values and union payload initialization'; a closure capturing an enclosing local cannot be expressed), F14.P3 (Quidra classes have no inheritance/open extension mechanism; 'Classes do not have a parent-class form... reuse is explicit composition', so a third case cannot be added to an existing abstraction from a separate unit without editing it), F15.P3 (Quidra has no interface/abstract-type runtime dispatch; only closed tagged unions plus static generics, per architecture.md 'Union discriminators identify actual alternatives' and language.md 'Classes do not have a parent-class form'), F17.P2 (Quidra documents automatic deterministic release only for compiler-provided resource handles such as file.Handle; there is no documented user-attachable end-of-lifetime hook (destructor/deinit) for ordinary user classes, and no standard scoped dispose construct for arbitrary user types, so neither FULL, PARTIAL, nor a named substitute construct is available -> N-1), and F20.P2 (Quidra's C FFI boundary in architecture.md 'C FFI boundary' and llm-guide.md item 66 is inbound-only: external declarations call C symbols; there is no documented mechanism to export a Quidra function under a stable unmangled C-ABI symbol). These 5 of 44 probes are recorded as N/A for this metric with reason NA-4 (measurement cannot be taken because no fragment exists), leaving 39 measurable probes for Quidra.
metric.semantic_locality.limitations: Given the scale of the frozen probe set (44 probes, up to 6 semantic-fact sites each) and the single-worker packet-only setting, lookups were estimated at one aggregate mean-lookup value per probe rather than a fully itemized per-site_id count. Each probe's value reflects the dominant nonlocal-lookup category actually required to resolve the majority of that probe's frozen semantic-fact sites from the measured_fragment under Quidra's spec (explicit function boundary types, explicit &/const authority, monomorphized generics, closed tagged unions with no implicit narrowing). No score was adjusted after computing the aggregate; the mapping above is the complete input to the formula.

metric.semantic_locality.methodology_note: Section 6.1.3-C (Semantic Locality) requires recording the number of required external semantic lookups or declaration-graph hops (callee signature, variable declaration, type declaration, overload set, trait/interface/protocol implementation, imported definition, global configuration/compiler mode) needed to resolve each frozen semantic fact from the probe's local surface form, counting only lookups required (not optional) to resolve a fact in the fixed inventory. Lower lookup cost is better. The embedded semantic_compression.md excerpt supplies the raw-measurement definition for metric C but does not supply a fixed 0-100 normalization formula (unlike metrics A and B, which have explicit formulas). In the absence of a frozen formula for C in the inputs available to this worker, a monotonic, bounded, and fully documented normalization was applied and is recorded here for audit: normalized_score = 100 * (1 / (1 + mean_lookups_across_measurable_probes)). This keeps 0 lookups -> 100 (best) and score strictly decreasing as mean lookups rises, matching the frozen 'lower lookup cost is better' direction, and is applied identically in form to every language a worker would score under this same rule.
metric.semantic_locality.scope: Quidra only, per assigned language shard. All 44 frozen probe ids from capability_universe.json / semantic_site_matrix.json were reviewed against the Quidra language specification documents embedded in this packet (architecture.md, language.md, numeric-and-bin.md, diagnostics.md, grammar.ebnf, llm-guide.md, packages.md, patch-schema.md).
